audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads "EVEN" while report[14] calls it a favoured matchup and diffRating says 4/10; the mirror audit (nasus__illaoi) settled Nasus's side at 7/10 HARD, whose inverse is 3/10 FAVOURED.
audit.why: 51.24% over 1409 games with Illaoi holding levels 1-6 is a favoured lane, and the two directions must not contradict.
audit.corrected: diff FAVOURED, diffRating 3/10, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] aligned to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed with the packet chart and with its own late-game text: phases[4]/win[4] said "Skill" at Level 6 and phases[6]/win[6] said "Illaoi" at 2+ items, while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say a stacked Nasus with Fury of the Sands out-sustains and out-damages you.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Illaoi through index 5 and Nasus at index 6; the mirror also has Illaoi winning Level 6. Level 6 is Leap of Faith (120s at rank 1) inside a tentacle field against a champion with no dash — Illaoi, not a coinflip.
audit.corrected: Level 6 -> Illaoi (rating 7/10) in both layers; 2+ items -> Nasus (rating 4/10) in both layers, proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the Sands was described only as "lifesteal-and-armor"; the page never says it grants bonus Armor AND Magic Resist while dealing percent-max-health damage, so stacking raw resistances is the wrong answer, nor that Grievous Wounds is the actual counter to Soul Eater lifesteal.
audit.why: Riot text on R: gains increased Health, Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown; flag percentHealth. Passive Soul Eater is lifesteal. Illaoi's own passive tentacles heal her, so the trade is a healing race Grievous Wounds decides.
audit.corrected: late rewritten to state armour/MR/percent-health and point at Executioner's Calling against Soul Eater.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset at 255 range and the page never gives the wind-up tell.
audit.why: His damage arrives on the auto animation, not the cast bar — reacting to the cast is reacting late.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now names the reset and the wind-up cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither's 700 range versus Harsh Lesson's 400 range was never stated, so "fight inside his W slow" had no mechanical reason attached.
audit.why: He can Wither you from outside your leap range; your answer is Test of Spirit at 900, which out-ranges Wither.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] now states the 700-vs-400 range gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. breakdown.cooldowns was generic boilerplate with no numbers.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, Test of Spirit 16/15/14/13/12s, Leap of Faith 120/95/70s — these turn "bait it" into a real timer.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with rank-1 numbers; dontsFull[1].d and dosFull[2].d given matching sequencing text.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wither and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 3/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wither and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Nasus carry threat 10/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 3/10, Nasus carry threat 10/10.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Bait it before committing. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nasus Wither: 15s at rank 1, 700 range — bait it out, then run the full pattern for 15 free seconds. - Your E is 16s at rank 1: whiff it and he stacks untouched. - Leap of Faith is 120s — kill windows only.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither is 15s: eat it, walk out, and commit when it comes back up.

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Each slam shoving him off the wave denies a Siphoning Strike.

edits.before: The one way you lose is scaling — a fully stacked Nasus with R becomes a lifesteal-and-armor juggernaut who heals through tentacle chip and out-DPS's you, so end it before Fury of the Sands carries him.
edits.after: The one way you lose is scaling — Fury of the Sands hands him armour, MR and percent-health damage, so more resistances are not the answer: Executioner's Calling cuts the Soul Eater lifesteal he heals through.

edits.before: You out-slam him while he's still under-stacked; keep the wave away from his tower and starve his Q so his scaling never arrives.
edits.after: His combo opens with a Siphoning Strike auto reset — the wind-up is your cue, not the cast. Punish it, and keep the wave off his tower.

edits.before: Use W (Wither) to slow your dash and kite the tentacles
edits.after: Wither you from 700 range to outrange your 400-unit leap

notes: Level chart flips proposed as one atomic group and paired across both layers (phases[4].side/win[4] Skill->Illaoi, phases[6].side/win[6] Illaoi->Nasus), matching the packet levelChart, the existing whys[6]/spikes[3]/late text, and the mirror. Ratings moved with them. diff EVEN->FAVOURED is an enum edit and reconciles the page with report[14] and with the mirror's 7/10 HARD on Nasus's side. Two things NOT proposed and left alone: (1) phases[4].why still says "Reassess every all-in at 6" which reads coinflip-ish next to an Illaoi-wins row, but rewriting it inside the length band adds no verified fact; (2) Test of Spirit tether-break rules — whether Cleanse/QSS or Fury of the Sands' unstoppable-like state affects the Vessel conversion is NOT in Riot's text, so wants.you[0]'s "no dash or cleanse to break tether" claim was left untouched and is recorded as unverified.
